label: Hiking, past the first summit
blurb: A walk stops being simple the moment you plan it. These are the directions the planning takes, and most of them happen indoors.

nodes.label: Day hikes
nodes.blurb: Up in the morning, back for dinner, one summit or a loop. The format everything else on this map quietly complicates.

nodes.label: Overnight and thru routes
nodes.blurb: The walk keeps going after dark, so the house comes along. Somewhere past the second night it stops being a hike and becomes a commute with views.

nodes.label: Map and compass
nodes.blurb: Contours, bearings and a plastic baseplate that never needs charging. Practised on clear days so it works on the day the cloud comes down.

nodes.label: GPX planning
nodes.blurb: Routes drawn at a desk the week before, elevation profile and all. Some of a walk's best hours happen at the computer, which nobody admits.

nodes.label: Trail snacks and water
nodes.blurb: Calories per gram, litres per hour and a firm position on jelly sweets. The menu gets planned harder than most dinner parties.

nodes.label: Footwear and blister craft
nodes.blurb: Boots or trail shoes, lacing patterns and tape applied before the hot spot, not after. Feet are the one piece of gear you cannot swap mid-walk.

nodes.label: Peak bagging
nodes.blurb: A published list of summits and a tick against each one. The hill was always there; the spreadsheet is what gets you out in November.

nodes.label: Night hikes
nodes.blurb: The same trail after dark, on a headtorch beam. Familiar paths stop being familiar, which is either the appeal or the warning.

nodes.label: Leave no trace
nodes.blurb: Pack it out, keep to the path, leave nothing to find. The one discipline here that is invisible when done well, which makes it hard to show off.

nodes.label: Hiking logs
nodes.blurb: Dates, routes, weather and who came along, kept for years. Reads as admin until the day you need to know which year the bridge washed out.

edges.note: One planned overnight is how a day hiker learns what their pack really weighs.
The first long descent teaches more about lacing than any shop fitting.
Multi-day routes turn navigation from an app into a skill.
Same headtorch and spare batteries. One packs it for camp chores, the other builds the whole walk around it.
The same route planned twice: once on paper that cannot die, once on a screen that can.
A list of summits is already a log; it just grows more columns.
